8.content: [Born vs Taught: Some witches are born into witch families (Nate, Eli), some are taught by an approved mentor (Cam), and some learn outside the rules (Julian at first). Being born into magic doesn't make a witch better; a practiced learner can beat a gifted slacker. Nate has a lingering prejudice against non-born witches, but he trained Julian himself.]

9.content: [Witch Council: Witch society forbids teaching magic to uninitiated humans; the legitimate route is an approved mentor or formal initiation. Nate bent the rule for Julian, who was legitimized later.]

10.content: [Magic: A discipline, not a fixed power. Branches: glamour/illusion, warding/binding, divination, elemental, restoration, transmutation, enchantment, ritual. Witches can study several but usually specialize. Nate: binding/wards/contracts. Julian: glamour. Eli: divination. Cam: fire/electricity. Magic does not stop witches from dying.]

11.content: [The Coven: Nate, Julian, Eli and Cam are close friends first, a coven second. Nate started it and is the unofficial leader, not the boss. Cam turned him down at first, then got pulled in and stayed for the friends. Cam joined after Nate found out about him at the video store and recruited him, much like {{user}}. They hunt demons and make terrible decisions together. {{user}} is not an official member.]

12.content: [Santa Aurelia: a coastal LA County suburb (about 46k people) in 2005. Santa Aurelia University, Aurelia Beach & Pier, surf shops, a dying mall, Blockbuster, and a diner open until 3 AM. Almost everyone is ordinary. It is not a Hellmouth. Demons thrive here anyway.]

13.content: [Demons: Beings from the Infernal Realms, in many species with different looks, abilities and diets. Not all are evil, smart or hostile; some live alongside humans and some act like supernatural wildlife. They are separate from witches and ghosts. Vampires are classified as lesser demons (they dislike sun but are still dangerous). Witches follow a god separate from the Devil, from an old agreement to fight demons. There is no morality clause, so not all witches are good. Most know this through stories and tradition.]

14.content: [Demon Disguises: Some demons pass as human through shapeshifting, glamour, naturally human looks, or possession. Mirrors, photos and sunlight do not automatically expose them. Some live among humans for decades with jobs and homes. Others cannot disguise themselves at all. Looking monstrous does not mean more dangerous.]

15.content: [Demon Drain: Many demons feed on emotions, vitality, ambient magic or dreams. Signs of a long infestation: plants withering, odd temperature changes, flickering lights, exhaustion or unease, weakened wards, animals avoiding an area. Some demons drop sigils in hidden places to drain an area on their behalf, so a sigil is often found at the center of a disturbance. Not every disturbance is a demon, and not every demon drains.]

16.content: [Incubi & Succubi: Convincing-looking demons tied to desire and attachment who feed on emotional or vital energy. Their charm is strong but is not mind control, and some exploit humans while others do not. Cambions: very rare human-demon children. They look human and their powers vary; many witches only know them from disputed records.]

17.content: [Common Demons: Imps are small, mischievous, often destructive; groups are dangerous. Possessors occupy a living host who stays a separate person, and killing the host is never the answer. Wraiths are half-incorporeal fear-feeders found in abandoned places that can look like hauntings. Predators hunt living things, often in remote places, and strength does not equal magical skill.]

18.content: [Ancient Demons: Some demons belong to old families and courts, with deep knowledge and influence, and some hold human identities in society. The Consecrated are extremely rare ancient demons whose true forms look like corrupted holy icons (crowns, halos, veils, masks, extra arms). Their holiness means nothing about their intent, and an unidentified one is treated as a severe threat.]

19.content: [Demon Rules: Demons often approach humans and witches with deals. Some can enter enforceable contracts, but many cannot grant wishes. Summoning does not guarantee obedience, and bindings fail when built wrong or used on something too strong. There is no universal weakness: salt, iron, sunlight and holy symbols are not reliably effective. Some demons can be killed, others can only be banished, and banishing is not permanent.]

keysecondary: how do you know it's a demon
20.content: [Demon Hunters: Hunters can be human, witch or something else, and a human can be an excellent hunter with no magic. Skill comes from experience, research and knowing the species. There is no single hunter organization. No witch can identify every demon, and an unfamiliar magical signature is not proof of a demon.]

key: what do you want in return
21.content: [Demon Bargains: Demons often approach struggling or curious people with deals that sound generous. The price is hidden in the terms: a favor, a memory, a year of luck, a name. Some cannot grant what they promise at all and are only baiting a contract. A signed deal is binding, so check the terms first. Nate's contract magic can read and sometimes break a weak one.]

22.content: [Demon Hotspots: Demons often settle in neglected or forgotten places in Santa Aurelia, like the old pier at night or a campus basement. Signs: dead plants, flickering lights, cold spots, animals avoiding it, a sigil hidden nearby. Locals just say the place feels off.]
